question: How old was he when he died? Where is he buried?

answers: Andrew Carnegie passed away on August 11, 1919, at the age of 83. He was laid to rest at Sleepy Hollow Cemetery in Sleepy Hollow, New York, specifically on the Arcadia Hebron plot of land at the intersection of Summit Avenue and Dingle Road.

history.content: A polder is an area of land that has been reclaimed from a body of water, such as a lake or a part of the sea. In the context of the economic history of the Netherlands between 1500 and 1815, polders were created by draining inland lakes using windmills and converting them into fertile arable land. Water engineering, developed by Leeghwater, made easier by building windmills faster with the help of inventions such as wind - powered sawmills.
How is Andrew Carnegie connected to the Netherlands?

Andrew Carnegie served as a major donor for then newly - established International Court of Arbitration's Peace Palace. He contributed $1,500,000 in 1903 for the erection of the Peace Palace at The Hague. At the dedication of the Peace Palace in The Hague, Carnegie predicted that the end of war was ' ' as certain to come, and come soon, as day follows night. ' '
What else did Andrew Carnegie give money too?

Andrew Carnegie made several significant donations, aside from contributing to the Peace Palace at The Hague. He established the Carnegie Hero Fund and donated $150,000 for a Pan-American Palace in Washington. His interest in music led him to fund construction of 7,000 church organs and built Carnegie Hall in New York City.

Towards the end of his life, he dedicated his fortune to supporting various causes, including local libraries, world peace, education, and scientific research. Some of the notable institutions he founded or supported are the Carnegie Corporation of New York, Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, Carnegie Institution for Science, Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland, Carnegie Hero Fund, Carnegie Mellon University, and the Carnegie Museums of Pittsburgh. He sponsored the expedition that discovered the remains of the dinosaur Diplodocus carnegiei in the Morrison Formation. Then there is the Carnegie Medal for best children's literature in the UK and the Carnegie Faculty of Sport and Education at Leeds Beckett University and many more causes.

Andrew Carnegie
Carnegie died on August 11 , 1919 , in Lenox , Massachusetts at his Shadow Brook estate , of bronchial pneumonia . He had already given away $350,695,653 ( approximately $76.9 billion , adjusted to 2015 share of GDP figures ) of his wealth . After his death , his last $30,000,000 was given to foundations , charities , and to pensioners . He was buried at Sleepy Hollow Cemetery in Sleepy Hollow , New York . The grave site is located on the Arcadia Hebron plot of land at the corner of Summit Avenue and Dingle Road . Carnegie is buried only a few yards away from union organizer Samuel Gompers , another important figure of industry in the Gilded Age .

Kyrie Irving
Irving was born on March 23 , 1992 in Melbourne , Australia , to American parents . He is the son of Drederick and Elizabeth Irving , and the stepson of Shetellia Irving . He has an older sister , Asia , and a younger sister , London . His father , Drederick , played college basketball at Boston University alongside Shawn Teague and under coach Rick Pitino . After completing his college career , Irving 's father moved to Australia to play professionally for the Bulleen Boomers . Irving lived in the Melbourne suburb of Kew before relocating to the United States when he was two years old . He holds dual American and Australian citizenship . Irving 's mother Elizabeth who was Sioux , died from an illness when he was four , so Drederick raised him with the help of Irving 's aunts .
